source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 7, 15-21; Instruction 16 standard deduction (PDF page 21); Instruction 10 and Exemption Amount Chart 10A (PDF pages 12-13); Instruction 17 Tax Rate Schedule II (PDF page 22); Chart 10A row '$100,000 or less ... $3,200' / joint column up to $150,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 150,000.00 = 150,000.00. Federal taxable income = 150,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 118,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 150,000.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 150,000.00. Line 14 two-income subtraction: 0.00 (the spouse has no income, Worksheet 13D line 6 is 0). Line 15 total subtractions 0.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 150,000.00 - 0.00 = 150,000.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 6,700.00. Line 18 net income = 150,000.00 - 6,700.00 = 143,300.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 150,000.00 (not over 150,000) gives 3,200.00 each x 2 (Box A) = 6,400.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 143,300.00 - 6,400.00 = 136,900.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule II as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 133,900.00 = 6,360.25; total 6,450.25. (Taxable net income is 100,000 or more, so the form uses Worksheet Schedules 17A, the same formula: 6,450.25.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 6,450.25. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000). Chart 10A: joint returns keep the full 3,200 at federal AGI of 150,000 or less; the first step applies only over 150,000.
